title: Advance Ruling under GST
outcomes: Identify questions on which an advance ruling can be sought.
Apply the procedure before the AAR.
Apply appeal, rectification and binding-effect rules.
Explain void rulings and the national appellate mechanism.

meta.exam_tip: Check first whether the question is in section 97(2) and not pending for the applicant.

concepts.title: Scope of advance ruling and authorities
body: An advance ruling is a binding decision by the Authority for Advance Ruling (AAR) or the Appellate Authority (AAAR) on listed questions about supplies proposed or already undertaken by the applicant. The applicant may be registered or seeking registration.

Questions allowed under section 97(2): classification; applicability of a notification; time and value of supply; admissibility of ITC; liability to pay tax; whether registration is required; and whether a particular activity amounts to a supply. Place of supply is outside the list.

Each State or UT has an AAR with one Central and one State member and an AAAR with the Chief Commissioner of Central Tax and the Commissioner of State tax. Rulings give certainty and help avoid costly disputes.
concepts.analogy: A pre-clearance on tax treatment, binding on both sides.
concepts.work: A start-up can ask whether its subscription bundle is a mixed supply before launch.

concepts.title: Procedure before the AAR
body: The application is made online with a fee of ₹5,000 each under CGST and SGST. The AAR sends a copy to the concerned officer, may call for records, and after hearing both sides passes an order admitting or rejecting it.
An application is rejected where the question is already pending or decided in proceedings concerning the applicant; rejection requires a speaking order after hearing.

Once admitted, the ruling must be pronounced within 90 days of receipt of the application after hearing both sides. If the two AAR members differ, the points go to the AAAR; if the AAAR members also differ, no ruling is given on that question.
concepts.analogy: Admission, hearing, ruling within ninety days.
concepts.work: A query already part of an audit notice for the applicant will be rejected.

concepts.title: Appeal, rectification and binding effect
body: The applicant, or the concerned or jurisdictional officer, may appeal to the AAAR within 30 days of receiving the ruling, extendable by another 30 days for sufficient cause. The AAAR decides within 90 days of filing after hearing the parties.

Under section 102, the AAR or AAAR may correct an error apparent on the record within 6 months of its order, on its own or when pointed out; if the correction raises tax or cuts ITC, the applicant must be heard first.

Under section 103, a ruling binds only the applicant and the concerned or jurisdictional officer for that applicant, and continues to bind until the law, facts or circumstances on which it rests change. It does not bind other similarly placed persons.
concepts.analogy: A ruling is personal to the applicant and lasts until the basis changes.
concepts.work: A competitor cannot rely on another firm's advance ruling as binding.

concepts.title: Void rulings and the national appellate mechanism
body: Section 104: where a ruling was obtained by fraud, suppression or misrepresentation of material facts, the authority may declare it void ab initio after hearing the applicant. The Act then applies as if no ruling existed, and the period from the ruling to the void order is excluded when computing limitation for demands.
Sections 101A to 101D provided for a National Appellate Authority to settle conflicting rulings of different States, but it was never set up.

From 1 April 2026, section 101A(1A) lets the Government, on Council recommendation, empower an existing authority, including a Tribunal, to hear such appeals in the interim; the study material notes the Principal Bench of the GST Appellate Tribunal for this role.
concepts.analogy: Rulings obtained by deception are wiped out retrospectively.
concepts.work: A ruling based on hidden facts about sales channels can be declared void.

viva.q: How long does an advance ruling stay binding?
viva.model: Until the law, facts or circumstances supporting the ruling change.

viva.q: What happens to limitation after a ruling is declared void?
viva.model: The period from the ruling to the void order is excluded when computing limitation.

viva.q: Who may appeal against an AAR ruling?
viva.model: The applicant, or the concerned or jurisdictional officer.
Because the national appellate body for conflicting rulings was never set up, the Government may empower an existing authority, including a Tribunal, to hear those appeals.

viva.q: Can a ruling be sought on an already completed transaction?
viva.model: Yes, rulings cover supplies proposed or already undertaken by the applicant.

cases.title: Ruling and later change
cases.case: Orchid Foods got a ruling that its packaged mix attracts 5% GST. A year later the rate notification is amended.

mcqs.q: Does the ruling still bind after the amendment?
mcqs.explain: Section 103(2). In practice: seek a fresh ruling.

mcqs.q: Can a competitor rely on this ruling as binding?
mcqs.explain: Personal ruling. In practice: persuasive only.
